name: Temporal re-scoring of weak candidates: Seq-NMS, REPP, tubelets, track-based confidence boost
essence: A single-frame detector scores each frame independently, so a real object whose score dips below threshold in one frame is lost even though it is confidently detected a few frames earlier or later. Temporal re-scoring links detections across frames into tubelets (by IoU, center distance, size ratio, class-vector similarity and optionally appearance) and replaces each detection's score with a tubelet statistic (Seq-NMS: average/max along the best path; REPP: mean class-confidence vector of the tubelet plus Gaussian smoothing of box coordinates). Tracker-side variants (ByteTrack second pass, BoostTrack DLO/DUO boost, BoostTrack++ soft boost, MR2-ByteTrack probabilistic rescore) raise a low-confidence detection when it agrees with an existing tracklet. Learned versions replace hand-made linking rules with a small classifier on pairwise temporal features. All of these work on already-computed detections, so they can be tested on the project's conf-0.01 caches without retraining the detector.
sources: Seq-NMS: Han et al., 'Seq-NMS for Video Object Detection', arXiv 1602.08465, 2016 (ILSVRC2015 VID 3rd place); public implementation inside FGFA code (MIT). REPP: Sabater, Montesano, Murillo, 'Robust and efficient post-processing for video object detection', IROS 2020, arXiv 2009.11050; code github.com/AlbertoSabater/Robust-and-efficient-post-processing-for-video-object-detection (GPL-3.0; appearance matching optional). BoostTrack: Stanojevic & Todorovic, Machine Vision and Applications 2024 (DOI 10.1007/s00138-024-01531-5). BoostTrack++: Stanojevic & Todorovic, arXiv 2408.13003 (2024), Filomat 39(16) 2025; code github.com/vukasin-stanojevic/BoostTrack (MIT). ByteTrack: Zhang et al., ECCV 2022, arXiv 2110.06864 (MIT). MR2-ByteTrack (Rescore): Bompani, Rusci, Palossi, Conti, Benini, CVPR 2024 Workshops (EVW), arXiv 2404.11488. SGT detection recovery: Hyun et al., WACV 2023, arXiv 2205.00968, github.com/HYUNJS/SGT. Feature-level temporal aggregation for comparison: YOLOV (Shi, Wang, Guo, AAAI 2023, arXiv 2208.09686) and YOLOV++ (arXiv 2407.19650, 2024), github.com/YuHengsss/YOLOV (Apache-2.0). Score refinement in 3D MOT: Benbarka et al., IROS 2021. Tracker-mined hard positives on BDD100K video: RoyChowdhury et al., CVPR 2019, arXiv 1904.07305. Project internal: dissertation/ЕДИНЫЙ_ПЛАН.md §2.5 (miss ladder, tracker ladder, threshold attempts), §3.6 (11-tracker zoo incl. BoostTrack/BoostTrack++ on the same cache), event_heads_v1 (q_det/q_birth heads), line_b_combined_v1.
fly_role: Role: evidence feature inside the temporal re-scorer, not the re-scorer itself. The tubelet re-scorer (Seq-NMS/REPP-style, IoU+geometry+class linking) carries the main mechanism; the fly adds a motion-consistency channel per candidate that a single-frame detector cannot see. What to read from the fly: (1) T4/T5 direction-selective energy (ReLU(T4a-d - baseline) + ReLU(T5a-d - baseline)) inside the candidate box versus a surrounding ring, already implemented in tracking/flyvis_activity.py (inside/ring, direction entropy, dominance, net vector); a real object moving relative to ego-flow should show coherent, persistent directional energy that differs from its ring, while a flicker/false positive from headlights, reflections or compression noise should show incoherent or ring-identical energy; (2) temporal persistence of that signature along the tubelet (direction stability across 30 Hz frames), which is exactly the 'temporal evidence' the earlier class/geometry/scene correction lacked; (3) retina-lamina front-end (Naka-Rushton photoreceptor adaptation tau 0.3 s + lamina center-surround, tracking/retina.py) is mandatory at night, because without it the fly read compression block noise as motion on the dark video (median |flow| 1.26 -> 0.36 px after photoreceptor stage). Where the fly is applied: on fovea eyes. Currently eyes exist only for tracker tracks; for weak candidates that never become tracks (the main loss), eyes must be spawned on persistent weak tubelets (e.g. >= 3 raw 30 Hz frames linked), which is the only design change to the fly pipeline. Why it is plausible: the project has shown fovea fly features carry real information versus shuffled (+0.0021 AP, CI > 0 in q_match), connectome topology matters (+0.044 AP vs shuffled), and the retina gain is fly-specific (DIS gets nothing from the retina). Why it may fail: in q_match the fly added nothing over DIS (+fovea T4T5 -0.0004 AP, CI through zero) and nonlinear heads did not change that; a flow-based control (DIS magnitude/direction coherence inside vs ring) may capture the same evidence. The honest framing is therefore 'the fly as a motion-saliency verifier of weak tubelets', compared against an identical DIS-feature verifier.
loss_mechanism_targeted: Primary: THRESHOLD (21.0% night vs 15.5% day at 960; the candidate exists with the right box but its confidence is under-estimated by +0.098 in the working band). Temporal re-scoring is precisely a mechanism that lifts real but low-scored candidates using neighbouring-frame evidence, and leaves BLINDNESS (4.5%, no candidate at conf 0.01) untouched by construction. Secondary: BIRTH (age 0 found 31% night vs 68% at age 10+, two thirds of the gap via threshold): online/causal boosting cannot help the very first frame because there is no history, but bidirectional or lagged re-scoring (Seq-NMS/REPP use future frames; a lag of 3-6 raw 30 Hz frames is less than one 5 Hz annotated frame) can lift the first appearance from later confident frames; this is the strongest argument for the offline/lagged variant. Also the tracker ladder shows ByteTrack's second pass rescues only 18 of 3622 objects because weak boxes only extend existing tracks and tracks are born only from strong boxes; a weak-only tubelet that persists over many raw frames is never exploited today. OCCLUSION at night (5.4x penalty): partially, since partially occluded objects flicker in score; risk of suppression of true neighbours in crowded scenes (71.1% object-frames occluded). SMALL objects (56.7% found): partially, small objects have the most score flicker, but linking by IoU is fragile for small fast boxes (REPP gains concentrated on fast motion: +10.8 mAP fast vs +5.8 slow on VID). OVEREXPOSURE: weakly; glare-induced false positives may be suppressed if they are temporally incoherent.
novelty_overlap: Temporal re-scoring itself is old and not claimable: Seq-NMS (2016), T-CNN tubelet re-scoring (2017), Seq-Bbox-Matching, REPP (2020), YOLOV/YOLOV++ feature aggregation (2023/2024), MR2-ByteTrack rescore (2024), BoostTrack/BoostTrack++ detection-confidence boost (2024), SGT detection recovery (2023), ByteTrack low-score association (2022). Tracker-based recovery of missed detections as pseudo-labels on BDD100K was done by RoyChowdhury et al. (2019). Insect-inspired motion front-ends for small-target detection in clutter exist (ESTMD: Wiederman et al., PLoS ONE 2008; Bagheri et al., Bioinspir. Biomim. 2017; Wang et al. STMD papers 2018-2020) and the photoreceptor+LMC front-end idea is Brinkworth & O'Carroll 2009, which the project's retina module already credits. No work found that uses a connectome-constrained whole-optic-lobe model (FlyVis, Lappalainen et al. Nature 2024) as a verifier of weak detection tubelets [uncertain: absence of evidence from a limited search, not proof]. cannot_claim: temporal re-scoring, tubelet linking, track-based confidence boost, retina-style adaptation front-end, and any claim that 'motion helps detection' in general. Possible claim only if measured: that connectome-derived T4/T5 readout adds verification power over an equal-information optical-flow control for weak night candidates.
author_results: Seq-NMS (VID, Faster R-CNN era): 3rd place ILSVRC2015 VID; exact gain over per-frame NMS not stated in abstract [uncertain]. Re-measured in REPP paper on ImageNet VID val with YOLOv3 (Darknet-53, 512x512, conf filter 0.005): base 68.59 mAP50 -> Seq-NMS 71.51 (+2.92), Seq-Bbox-Matching 74.19 (+5.60), REPP 75.06 (+6.47); by motion speed REPP slow 76.79->82.54, medium 66.45->74.29, fast 45.79->56.58; post-processing cost 2.58 ms/frame (REPP) vs 10.41 ms (Seq-NMS) on RTX 2080Ti. REPP on video detectors: FGFA 77.1->80.09, SELSA 82.69->84.21 (no appearance features). Baselines are weak by 2026 standards (YOLOv3, R-FCN, Faster R-CNN R101); ImageNet VID has ~1.59 objects/frame, densely labelled, mostly hand-held or static cameras, 25-30 fps. YOLOV (AAAI 2023, feature aggregation, requires training): YOLOX-S 69.5 -> YOLOV-S 77.3 AP50, YOLOX-X 77.8 -> YOLOV-X 85.5, +post-processing 87.5; YOLOV++ FocalNet-L 92.9 (93.2 with post) on VID. MR2-ByteTrack (ImageNet VID subset with 16 COCO classes, 392 videos): NanoDet-Plus 42.70 -> 46.57 mAP, YOLOX-Nano 41.30 -> 46.47; the probabilistic Rescore contributes about +3.08 mAP beyond plain ByteTrack linking. BoostTrack++ (MOT17/MOT20, pedestrians, YOLOX from Deep OC-SORT): ablation on validation with BoostTrack+ baseline, no DLO -> full S+SB+VT: MOT17 HOTA 72.17 -> 72.22 (+0.05), MOTA 81.02 -> 81.33; MOT20 HOTA 62.59 -> 63.16 (+0.57), MOTA 77.16 -> 78.02; original DLO boost on SORT (MOT20 val): HOTA 56.65 -> 58.58, MOTA 69.91 -> 73.28 but IDs +8% and IDSW +12%. Test: BoostTrack++ HOTA 66.6 (MOT17), 66.4 (MOT20). ByteTrack on BDD100K MOT: mMOTA 36.6 -> 45.5 (val) and 35.5 -> 40.1 (test) relative to prior leaderboard methods (not an ablation of low-score boxes alone). SGT: large MOTA gains on MOT20 and HiEve from recovering sub-threshold detections; exact numbers not verified here [uncertain]. RoyChowdhury 2019 (BDD100K pedestrians, clear-day -> rest incl. night, Faster R-CNN R50): source 15.21 AP -> detector pseudo-labels 26.16 -> tracker hard positives (HP) 27.11. Project's own measurement of tracker-side boosting on the same cache (50 val videos, threshold 0.25, no ReID): BoostTrack++ HOTA 43.33 / DetA 37.48 and BoostTrack 43.20 / 37.48 vs BoT-SORT DetA 42.26 and HybridSORT HOTA 47.78 / DetA 40.23, i.e. the confidence boost did not lift DetA above simpler trackers in this domain (after removing the pedestrian aspect-ratio filter that discarded 21.6% of GT).
strong_baseline_check: Weakly established. (1) Offline re-scoring gains shrink as the base detector gets stronger and already uses temporal context: REPP gives +6.5 mAP on YOLOv3 but +1.5 on SELSA; YOLOV++ gains only +0.3 from post-processing (92.9 -> 93.2). (2) On a strong modern tracker baseline, track-based confidence boosting is close to zero on sparse scenes (BoostTrack++ MOT17 val +0.05 HOTA) and meaningful only in dense pedestrian crowds (MOT20 +0.57 HOTA), with an identity cost (more IDs/IDSW). (3) In this project the one-frame version of the same evidence has already failed: the q_det head with tracklet-overlap context (ctx_max_iou_tracked, ctx_tracks_near) and one-step DIS link (dis_prev_max_iou) gave AP 0.9190 -> 0.9197, CI [-0.016; +0.007]; class/geometry/scene correction gave AUC 0.9025 -> 0.9005; lowering the night threshold 0.25 -> 0.15 gained detections but cost +169 ID switches; ByteTrack's second pass rescued 18/3622 objects; BoostTrack/BoostTrack++ on the same cache did not beat simpler trackers on DetA. What has NOT been tested here is the multi-frame (>= 3-6 raw frames), bidirectional/lagged tubelet statistic on the full 30 Hz stream for candidates that never become tracks. Equal-information control: the rescorer with IoU/geometry/DIS-only features is the control for the fly channel; for the tubelet idea itself the control is the frozen tracker with the threshold re-tuned to the same FP budget. No independent reproduction of REPP on driving data with a modern NMS-free detector was found [uncertain].
conditions_breakdown: REPP and YOLOV break down only by object speed (slow/medium/fast) on ImageNet VID; REPP also tests reduced frame rates (sparse sampling), where it alone always stays above baseline. BoostTrack++ breaks down by dataset density (MOT17 vs MOT20). No night/overexposure/occlusion/small-object or first-appearance breakdown in any of these papers, and none on BDD100K MOT [uncertain for SGT]. RoyChowdhury 2019 reports BDD100K sub-domains (night, rain, fog etc.) for pedestrian adaptation. The project itself has the needed strata (night/day, age 0 vs 10+, occluded, size) in the miss ladder and event datasets.
cheap_gate: Gate T0, no fly, CPU only, about 1-2 hours. Data: runs/det_cache_ctl_960 (all 200 val videos, 5 Hz, conf 0.01, iou 0.7, imgsz 960) and runs/video_rate (the 7 val videos, val7, with detections on every raw 30 Hz frame, content-aligned to labelled frames). Variants applied to the cached candidates: (a) Seq-NMS (class-aware max-path linking at IoU > 0.5, average re-score, without its suppression step so that crowded neighbours are not deleted); (b) REPP-lite (logistic link score on IoU, centre distance, w/h ratios, class-vector dot product; tubelet mean re-score; no appearance), using REPP's published config as a starting point and fitting the link classifier on train/dev videos only; (c) causal EMA tubelet score (online); (d) lagged tubelet score with a 3-6 raw frame look-ahead. Measurements on labelled val frames, split night/day, age 0 / 1-9 / 10+, occluded / not, size: per-class AP and mAP50 of re-scored detections; the share of THRESHOLD-step objects (GT matched by a candidate with conf in [0.01, 0.25)) lifted above 0.25 at a fixed added-FP budget per frame; then the frozen line_b_combined_v1 tracker on re-scored detections (val7 first, then test 35 only if val passes): DetA, FN, FP, IDSw, HOTA, with video-level bootstrap CIs. Pre-registered thresholds (write into the card before running): night threshold-step recovery >= +3 pp absolute at equal FP budget with bootstrap 95% CI > 0; DetA on val7 >= +0.3 with CI excluding 0 and not worse by day; IDSw not worse than +5%; stop if recovery < 2 pp or the gain equals what simple threshold re-tuning to the same FP budget gives. Gate T1, fly channel, only if T0 passes, a few GPU hours: spawn retina-lamina fovea eyes on persistent weak tubelets in runs/video_rate videos, read T4/T5 inside/ring energy and direction stability, add to the T0 re-scorer; compare against the same re-scorer with DIS-flow inside/ring features, shuffled-fly and connectome-null controls (existing scripts compare_connectome_null.py and the fovea readout cache). Criterion: night band-candidate AUC gain over the DIS re-scorer larger than the split-based plank (as in q_gate1, plank 0.0081) and threshold-step recovery +1 pp with CI > 0; otherwise record completed_negative for the fly channel while keeping the tubelet result.
cost_here: No detector training at all. T0 on existing caches: minutes to about 1 hour CPU for linking and re-scoring over 200 val videos, plus TrackEval on val7/test35 (minutes each). Full 30 Hz evidence requires a new detection cache on raw video: only 7 val videos are stored locally (data/bdd100k/videos/val), while all 1400 train-split videos are local (data/bdd100k/videos/train), so the 30 Hz gate should run on the project's held-out dev/test videos from the train split (as line_b_combined_v1 already does) or the 200 val videos must be downloaded first (needs the user's permission). Cost estimate: the 5 Hz 200-video cache took 22 min, so about 6x frames gives roughly 2-2.5 h GPU at 960 per 200 videos [uncertain: extrapolated]. Fly fovea eyes on weak tubelets: fly signatures ran at about 75 ms/frame per video with the existing eye bank; for the 7 val7 videos at 30 Hz (~8k frames) about 15-30 min, for all 200 val videos about 5 h (overnight, Idle priority) [uncertain: depends on eye count per frame]. Inference cost of REPP-style post-processing is a few ms per frame (2.58 ms reported for REPP on 2080Ti); a lagged variant adds 100-200 ms latency. A learned feature-level temporal detector (YOLOV-style) would instead need full training: about 4.3 h per 12-epoch run, at least 3 seeds per arm, 100-epoch confirmation about 35 h per run.
expected_effect: Detection AP (per-frame mAP50 on labelled frames): plausible +1 to +3 points overall, larger at night, by analogy with REPP/Seq-NMS gains on a moderately strong single-frame detector (YOLOv3 +2.9 to +6.5 on VID) discounted for the stronger YOLO26 and lower object persistence in driving [uncertain]. Tracker DetA: smaller, about +0.2 to +0.8 on test, because the tracker already integrates temporal evidence for existing tracks and the measured tracker-side boost (BoostTrack family) and one-frame context (q_det) gave nothing; the remaining room is the weak-only tubelets and the first-appearance frames (age 0), which only the lagged/bidirectional variant can address [uncertain]. Upper bound reference: lifting all threshold-step objects at night would recover 21.0 - 15.5 = 5.5 pp of the night-day gap; realistically a fraction of that. Fly channel: expected near zero over a DIS-feature re-scorer (prior evidence +0.000 to +0.005 AP over DIS in matching tasks); a positive, night-specific contribution of the retina-lamina fly is possible on small/occluded candidates where coherent motion is the only evidence, but should be treated as a hypothesis [uncertain].
risks: Lessons from DRB do not apply directly (no training, so no seed noise of 0.0144 mAP and no sign flip with epochs), but analogous traps exist: (1) tuning re-scoring thresholds on the same val videos used for the verdict; fit link classifiers and thresholds on train/dev only, judge on val7/test35 with bootstrap by video; (2) comparing an offline/lagged method with an online tracker without labelling it as such; BDD100K MOT evaluation does not forbid offline processing, but claims must state the latency; (3) identity cost: lifting weak candidates historically added ID switches (+169 when lowering the night threshold; BoostTrack DLO +12% IDSW); (4) suppression step of Seq-NMS can delete true neighbours in occluded crowds (71.1% object-frames occluded) and must be disabled or tested separately; (5) class heterogeneity: bus confidence is over-estimated at night (-0.20...-0.40) while car/pedestrian are under-estimated, so re-scoring must be per-class; (6) domain defaults: BoostTrack's pedestrian aspect-ratio filter silently removed 21.6% of GT; REPP/Seq-NMS defaults were tuned on ImageNet VID at 25-30 fps with few objects; (7) frame-rate mismatch: 5 Hz labels vs 30 Hz video; linking at 5 Hz is IoU-fragile for small fast objects; (8) fly-specific: eyes are per-track today; spawning eyes on weak tubelets changes coverage and must be identical across fly and DIS arms; FlyVis is slow (float32 only) and the earlier fly features did not add over DIS; (9) licences: REPP is GPL-3.0 (reimplement rather than vendor its code), BoostTrack MIT, YOLOV Apache-2.0, FGFA Seq-NMS MIT.
attribution: Borrowed and cited: tubelet linking and re-scoring (Seq-NMS, Han et al. 2016; REPP, Sabater et al. IROS 2020; T-CNN), track-based confidence boosting (BoostTrack/BoostTrack++ 2024; ByteTrack 2022; MR2-ByteTrack 2024), tracker-mined hard positives (RoyChowdhury et al. 2019), photoreceptor+LMC front-end idea (Brinkworth & O'Carroll 2009), FlyVis model and weights (Lappalainen et al., Nature 2024). Project's own: the diagnosis that the night deficit sits in the threshold step and the birth frame, the gate design on conf-0.01 caches with the threshold-step recovery metric, the lagged/bidirectional variant targeted at age-0 objects, the retina-lamina implementation (own simplified code), the fovea-eye readout of T4/T5 for weak tubelets, and the equal-information DIS/shuffled/connectome-null controls. If the fly channel does not beat the DIS control, the tubelet re-scorer is reported as an engineering application of known methods, not as novelty.
